# AI agent Settings

**Since mid-to-late August 2026, the AI agent page is a hub, not one long settings
screen.** Go to **AI agent** in the app menu to land on the hub, which groups every
sub-page under four headings: *What the AI knows* (Training data, Shop memory),
*How the AI behaves* (Instructions, **Skills**, **Scenarios**), *How the AI is doing*
(unresolved questions, Chatty Lab), and *Where the AI works* (**Settings**). Each of
those is now its own page with its own URL — "AI agent → Settings" below means
clicking the **Settings** card from that hub, not a tab inside a longer page.

Configure your AI agent's identity, availability, and channels at **AI agent →
Settings**. Use the **Test AI** button at the top right to preview behavior without
affecting live chat.

> **Looking for Custom Scenarios or Assistant skills (Human handover, After-sales
> support, Product recommendations, etc.)?** Those moved out of this page entirely —
> see **AI agent → Scenarios** and **AI agent → Skills** respectively. This file only
> covers what's still on the Settings page itself: identity, availability,
> re-engagement, follow-up, channels, and embed placement.

## Use Chatty as Human-Only Live Chat (Turn Off AI)

If a merchant wants to use Chatty as a pure human live chat tool with no AI involvement
at all, the answer is simple — **just deactivate the AI agent**. There is no need to
turn off AI channels one by one.

- **If the AI agent is on** → go to **AI agent** (in the app left menu), then click the
  **Deactivate** button at the top right of the page (next to Settings and Test AI).
  Once deactivated, all incoming conversations go straight to your inbox for your team
  to handle manually, and customers see no AI — the AI name and avatar only appear while
  the AI is actively responding.
- **If the AI agent was never activated** → just leave it **disabled** (the default).
  Nothing else needs to be done.

To turn AI back on later, click **Activate** on the same AI agent page.

## AI Identity

Customize the AI's name and avatar, shown to customers in conversations.
Path: **AI agent → Settings**.

- **Name**: The name shown to customers in the chatbox. Set it at
  **AI agent → Settings → Name**.
- **Avatar**: Choose a preset avatar, or upgrade to upload a custom image
- **Welcome message**: The first message customers see. Click **Insert customer name**
  to personalize it with the customer's name.

### Which "name" does the merchant mean? (three different fields)

Chatty has three separate name/identity fields. Identify which one the merchant is
pointing at before giving a path — a screenshot usually makes it obvious.

| What they want to change | Where it lives | What it affects |
|---|---|---|
| **AI agent name** — the name customers see when the AI replies | **AI agent → Settings → Name** | The AI's display name in the chatbox |
| **Team member / operator name** — the name on a human agent's profile | **Settings → Team → Manage** (edit the member) | The name customers see when a human replies |
| **Role / persona instructions** — how the AI describes itself and behaves | **AI agent → Instructions → General instructions → Role** | The AI's tone and self-description, **not** its display name |

**Common request — "make the AI introduce itself as our brand, not as an AI / not as
Chatty":** this is two settings working together.

1. Set the display name at **AI agent → Settings → Name** to the brand name.
2. Describe the persona at **AI agent → Instructions → General instructions →
   Role** (e.g. "You are the support assistant for BRAND").

Changing the Role text alone does **not** change the display name — the name field is
what customers see on the message.

### Which "welcome message" does the merchant mean? (four places)

The most common "I changed it but the old message still shows" case. Three of these override one another — check in this order — and the fourth (**First auto-reply**) is a separate message that is sent on top of them, not an override:

| Field | Where it lives | When it applies |
|---|---|---|
| **Chatbox welcome message** | **Legacy chatbox → General → Welcome Message** | Used only when the AI agent is **off** |
| **AI welcome message** | **AI agent → Settings → AI identity → Welcome message** | Used when the AI agent is **on** — overrides the chatbox one. Supports `{{customer_name}}` |
| **Translated welcome message** | **Settings → Translations → [language] → AI Agent / Live chat** | Each published language keeps its own copy — overrides **both** of the above for visitors in that language |
| **First auto-reply (Online / Offline message)** | **Settings → General → Chat availability → Manage → First auto-reply** | A **separate** automatic first message, not an override. Default online text is "Thank you for reaching out. We'll be with you in a moment"; default offline text is "We are currently offline. We will respond as soon as possible during our next business hours". See `faq_online-hours.md` |

If the AI is enabled, the merchant needs to edit the **AI welcome message**. If they also have translations published, the translated copy is the most common reason an edit "doesn't take" — it must be updated separately. Note a separate **Proactive Chat** campaign message can also appear as a pop-up teaser; that one is edited in the **Proactive chat** section, not here.

**If the merchant quotes "Thank you for reaching out. We'll be with you in a moment" (or a similar
"we'll be with you shortly" line), it is the First auto-reply → Online message** under
**Settings → General → Chat availability → Manage**. Do **not** send them to Human handover: the
**Response time promise** field is set on the **Human handover** scenario — edit it at
**AI agent → Scenarios → Human handover** (the same setting shows as a **Human agent transfer**
status row on **AI agent → Skills → Customer support** — same setting, different page,
different label, see `faq_human-handover.md`) — shown only after a handover to the
"Collect info & follow up by email" destination. Two different messages, two different screens.

**The AI welcome message is the same across every channel.** Website chat, WhatsApp, Messenger, Instagram, and email all use the one AI welcome message (or, for a visitor in a published language, that language's translated version). There is **no setting to configure a different greeting per channel** — you cannot give WhatsApp a different opening line from the website widget. If a merchant wants a distinct greeting for one channel only, the only lever available today is language/translation, not channel; there is no per-channel override.

### "AI Not Using the Identity I Gave It"

If a merchant reports the AI isn't using the identity they configured, start at
**AI agent → Settings** and verify Name/Avatar/Welcome message are saved, and check
**AI agent → Instructions → General instructions → Role** for the persona text. Don't default
to the generic data-source/Instructions-saved troubleshooting used for wrong-answer
cases (see `case_ai-wrong-responses` → *AI Reverts to Default Behavior*) — that flow
is for factual answers, not identity/persona.

## Support Email Addresses

Set a **Contact support email**. The customer contact form and chat history are
sent to this address. Separate multiple emails with commas (,).

## AI Availability — Control When AI Replies

Control when the AI agent replies to customers, based on your team's availability.

Go to **AI agent → Settings → AI availability → Choose when AI replies**, then pick:

- **Always** — AI replies anytime, even when agents are online
- **Only when agents are offline** — AI replies only when no human agents are online

Manage your team's hours in **Chat availability settings**.

**No time-based failover exists.** There is no setting to have the AI automatically take over if a human doesn't reply within N minutes while still inside business hours — availability is schedule-based only (Always vs. Only when agents are offline). Workaround for coverage gaps during working hours: set the online-status display rule (**Settings → Working hours → Online status display**) to treat the team as "offline" whenever no agent is actually online, even inside business hours, so the AI can still catch chats. Log a request for true time-based failover as a feature request if a merchant specifically needs it.

## AI Re-engagement

**AI re-engage after resolution**: When enabled, resolved conversations are reopened
and reassigned to the AI when a customer sends a new message. Respects your AI
availability setting.

## Follow-up Messages

**AI Follow-up**: Automatically sends a follow-up when a customer goes silent during
a conversation, helping recover distracted shoppers.

- **Wait time**: How long to wait after the customer's last message before sending a
  follow-up. Choose from a dropdown: **3 minutes**, **5 minutes (recommended)**,
  **10 minutes**, or **15 minutes** (default: 5 minutes).

## AI Channels

**Out of the box the AI only answers on the online store chat widget.** Every other channel starts
switched off, even after it has been connected successfully. Connecting WhatsApp, Messenger,
Instagram or Email brings the messages into the Inbox, but the AI stays silent on them until that
channel is turned on here as well.

This is the usual explanation for *"the AI replies on my website but not on WhatsApp/Messenger/email"* —
the channel is connected, it just was never added to the list the AI is allowed to answer on. Check
this before treating it as a fault.

Enable the **AI agent to reply** on selected channels: **Email**, **Messenger**,
**Instagram**, and **WhatsApp**. Click **Connect** on each channel to set it up.

The **Pro/Plus** plan gate applies to **AI auto-reply on that channel** — not to
connecting the channel itself. Connecting WhatsApp, Messenger, Instagram, or Email
is available on **all plans, including Free**; only having the AI respond
automatically on WhatsApp, Messenger, or Instagram requires **Pro or Plus** (see
`case_whatsapp-messenger-issues` and `faq_channels`).

## Embed Product AI Agent

**AI product assistant**: Configure how your AI agent behaves and responds to customer
questions about your products, embedded on your product pages. Use **Go to theme** to
add it (this enables the theme app embed — it does NOT open cart settings). Available
on the **Pro** and **Plus** plans.

Note: there is no separate "Add-to-Cart" toggle or setting. Adding items to the cart is
automatic behavior of the AI product assistant — the AI adds an item when a customer
asks in chat. If a merchant reports the AI isn't adding items to cart, treat it as a
support case (theme compatibility / variant issue), not a setting to enable — see
kb_ai-wrong-responses.

## Embed Homepage AI Agent

**AI agent on Homepage**: Embed the AI chat widget on your homepage so customers can
ask about your store, find products, and get instant AI responses. Use **Go to theme**
to add it. Available on the **Pro** and **Plus** plans.


## AI Agent Actions (AI Doing Real Tasks for a Customer)

**Moved off this page.** These toggles used to live here; they now live at
**AI agent → Skills → Customer support**, alongside Order tracking and Human agent
transfer — see `faq_ai-training-setup` → *AI Capabilities & Limits* for the merchant-facing
summary of what the AI can do.

Since **13/08**, the AI agent can take two limited actions directly on a customer's order/account instead of only collecting info and handing off to a human:

- **Change shipping address** — only on orders that **haven't shipped yet**. Once an order has shipped or been cancelled, the AI cannot change it and will say so, offering a human handover instead.
- **Update email subscription** — opt a customer in or out of marketing emails.

**Setup:** each action is a **separate toggle row** on **AI agent → Skills → Customer support**, both **default OFF**. A merchant must explicitly turn on each one they want the AI to be allowed to do — enabling one does not enable the other.

**Identity check before acting:** the AI only performs the action after the customer clearly confirms it in the preceding message.
- **Logged-in customers** are matched automatically against their account.
- **Guest/anonymous customers** must provide the exact **email or phone number on the order** — if it doesn't match, the AI refuses and does not reveal any order details.

**What the AI still cannot do here:** cancel an unshipped order, or take any account-authentication action (login help, OTP, password reset — see `faq_ai-training-setup` → *AI Capabilities & Limits*). Cancel-order exists in the code as a built action but is **deliberately withheld from release** — it's the one irreversible action (no un-cancel in Shopify) and its refund/restock behavior isn't yet merchant-configurable. A third toggle for AI-initiated password reset was tested but was **removed on 18/08** and is not available to merchants.

**No admin log yet** — there is currently no screen in the app to review what the AI changed on a customer's behalf. If a merchant asks "did the AI actually update my customer's address," this has to be checked with the team; it isn't self-serve yet.

## Pricing Display Rules (Hide a Price / Show "Call for Price" Instead)

**Since 11/09**, a merchant can configure the AI's product card (shown inside a chat conversation) to hide a product's real price and show a contact-style label instead — for products where the real price only exists once a human sets it (made-to-order, custom quotes, wholesale-only pricing, etc.).

**Location:** **AI agent → Skills → Pricing display rules** (linked from the Skills page).

**How it works — three parts, all under one toggle:**

1. **Pricing display rules** toggle (default **off**). Off = every product shows its real price, as it always has. On = any product matching the rule below shows the label instead.
2. **Which products match** — a product matches when **any one** of these is true:
   - **Products priced at zero** — catches products the merchant intentionally priced at `$0` because the real price is quoted by hand (without this rule they'd otherwise show "$0.00" to the customer).
   - **Product tags** — comma-separated list of tags.
   - **Product types** — comma-separated list of product types.
3. **What shoppers see on a matching product's chat card** — the **Add to Cart button is hidden**, and the price is replaced by one of these merchant-chosen options:
   - **Call for Price** (default label)
   - **Contact for pricing**
   - **Price on request**
   - **Request a quote**
   - **Hide the price** — removes the price entirely, no replacement label

**Scope:** this only changes the product card the AI shows **inside a chat conversation** (AI Mode / live chat). It does **not** touch the merchant's storefront theme or product pages — the real price still shows there exactly as before. A matching product also **cannot be added to cart or bought through the AI conversation** at all once the rule is on for it — the block is enforced by checking the product's actual catalog data, not by instructing the AI to avoid it.

**What this does NOT do:** it does not create a quote-request form, does not generate a quote/proposal, and does not create a Shopify draft order. It only changes what the AI's chat product card displays and blocks the cart button — if a customer wants to actually negotiate or receive a price, the AI still just falls back to whatever handoff/contact flow the merchant has configured elsewhere (see `faq_human-handover`). Don't tell a merchant this builds them a quoting workflow — as of September 2026 that capability doesn't exist yet.
